name: JW Marriott Starr Pass Resort and Spa
positioning: Sonoran Desert golf and spa resort in Tucson (officially JW Marriott Tucson Starr Pass Resort & Spa), with 27 holes of desert golf and a lazy river
best_for: Golfers who want desert courses with history
Families who want a complimentary lazy river and water slide
Travelers who want desert rituals, hikes and a spa

facts.text: The resort sits in a desert setting in Tucson, Arizona.
The Palmer Course nine at The Club at Starr Pass was designed by Arnold Palmer.
The Club at Starr Pass hosted the Tucson Open from 1987 to 1996, and Phil Mickelson won it there as an amateur in 1991.
The Club at Starr Pass is a Certified Audubon Cooperative Sanctuary.
The collection of outdoor water features is complimentary for guests.
Private cabanas can be rented by the pool for shade.
Hashani Spa has a saline lap pool.
Some rooms have a patio or balcony with lazy river, mountain, golf or desert views.
The resort runs a daily guided morning hike through the Sonoran Desert.
Salud is an outdoor restaurant serving authentic Mexican cuisine, hand-crafted cocktails and fine tequilas.
Signature Grill serves Southwestern cuisine featuring Native American and Mexican dishes.
Nearby activities include Saguaro National Park and Old Tucson.

highlights.text: The Club at Starr Pass offers 27 holes of championship desert golf, and the Pioneer Course's sixth fairway follows Richard Starr's original trail.
The water collection includes the Starr Canyon lazy river, the Monsoon Falls water slide and the Reflection Pools.
Hashani Spa combines modern beauty and health technology with ancient healing techniques inspired by the region's indigenous people.
Each morning guests can join a traditional Native American ceremony on the Salud Terrace, and every evening at sunset they gather there for a tequila toast.
All rooms have plush bedding, marble bathrooms, sitting areas and flat-screen TVs.

considerations.text: Pets are not allowed at the resort.
The resort charges a resort fee, which covers amenities including the daily rituals.
WhataHotel notes the resort location requires transportation to downtown Tucson attractions.
